_note: Draft 7 (2026-10-12), not frozen. Fixed before any data was acquired. The researcher chose among Claude's options in .steering/20261012-public-keystroke-matching-prereg/decisions.md: decisions 8-15 (design; in decisions 8 and 10 the researcher chose an option other than Claude's recommendation), decisions 16-23 (attack-me round 1), 24-25 (paper repository; OSF registration and Zenodo release) 26-31 (attack-me round 2), 32-36 (attack-me round 3), 37-40 (attack-me round 4) and 41-47 (the synthetic-log check before freezing and its review). The numbers are Claude's proposals adopted by the researcher. These are experiment values, not pass criteria. If this file and the Japanese draft disagree, the frozen English version is authoritative.

registration.code_and_aggregates: Zenodo release of the paper repository (decisions 24, 25)
registration.data: not redistributed; obtained from each source

tools.keytar: defaults of the released artifact; recorded in data.md at check 6

writer_id: string of the distributed ID column, used verbatim in the seed derivation
seed_derivation: int.from_bytes(sha256(f'{SEED}:{use}:{prompt}:{writer}:{N}:{k}:{draw}'.encode()).digest()[:8], 'big') -> numpy.random.default_rng; unused fields are empty strings

klicke.acquisition_condition: researcher decided to proceed after reading the authors' reply (decisions 4, 7)
klicke.files: to be filled at acquisition: Drive file IDs, SHA-256, GitHub commit
do_not_acquire: demographics (record the zip SHA-256 only if bundled; do not extract)
klicke.active_window: first keypress to the last event whose text_change is non-empty (R0), applied to every form

enja15.acquisition_condition: license type and terms checked in the primary source (decisions 5, 7)
enja15.sessions: T (from-scratch translation); meaning of T/P/D to be confirmed in [P273]/[P359] before acquisition

key_categories_detail.navigation: other movement keys (ArrowUp, ArrowDown, PageUp, PageDown)

key_categories_note: navigation and modifier split after the synthetic-log check (decisions 42, 43)
shortcut_rule: a letter or digit press (in R3-u: a char press, since letters and separators are merged) is a shortcut (not counted, not a separator, and it breaks the A3 chain of consecutive char presses) when it is the next press other than control/modifier after a control press; the held state cannot be read because the modifier action time is 0 ([V264] 2.1.5) (decision 43)

R3.time: down_time only; up_time and action_time dropped (decision 41); a drag's or held key's duration stays as a lower bound of the next press interval (decision 44, limitation)

R3-u.keys: category with letter/digit/space/punctuation/enter merged into char

R3-t.floored: down_time (the only time column of R3)

R6.keys: alnum identities of typed presses (Input and the typed side of Replace) permuted within segment
R6.text_change: same permutation for typed characters; letters and digits of strings that do not come from a press (pasted, replaced and removed text) masked to q as in R1 (decision 46)

columns_not_in_table: dropped in every form except R0 (e.g. Pause Time); no time-derived column is kept or recomputed

alignment.ties: earlier group in the list; at the end, the smallest text position
alignment.end_window: record fully used, text may end early
alignment.end_full_text: record and text both fully used
alignment.no_path: cost infinity; all infinite -> tie among all
report_infinite: only the true text infinite while a decoy is finite
alignment.r7_group_cap: ceil(3 / (1 - p)) for (1,q) and (p',1): 4 at p = 0.1 and 0.25, 6 at p = 0.5; fixed (decisions 26, 33); the synthetic-log check reports the share of true groups above the cap and the cost inflation of the true text
alignment.implementation: align.py from experiments/20261011-g1-copy-self-trial/scripts implements the window end only; full-text end, infinity reporting and the R7 groups are added as a wrapper (replace the group list and call with max_group = 4 or 6; the default is 3) and checked on synthetic logs before freezing

split.rule: train on one pair of prompts, evaluate on the other, then swap; every writer is evaluated once; decoys never include a training writer (decision 29)

attackers.train_on: all writers of the other fold's two prompts

A0.R4: record segment-value sum vs candidate sum of floor(value / w)

A1p.replay: char categories insert at the cursor; backspace deletes left, delete right; arrow_left/arrow_right move one; home/end move to the line start/end (lines split by enter); after a control press, home/end go to the document start/end and arrow_left/arrow_right are uncertain (cursor to the end) (decision 47); navigation (other movement keys) and mouse put the cursor at the end; shortcuts (shortcut_rule) are ignored (decision 42)

A2b.boundary_model: logistic regression (scikit-learn 1.5.2, L2, C = 1.0, solver lbfgs, max_iter 1000, class_weight none, threshold 0.5)
A2b.preprocessing: features standardised with the training mean and SD; a missing interval at the first or last presses is filled with the training median
features: log interval to the previous press
log interval to the next press

A3.fallback: a character pair seen fewer than 20 times takes the value of its character-type pair; a type pair seen fewer than 20 times takes the value of all intervals (found in the synthetic-log check)
A3.R3-u: combined score = mean per-term timing log-likelihood + length log-likelihood (decisions 27, 32). A1' replay (Home and End also treated as uncertain, cursor to the end, because Enter is merged into char) gives the final char sequence, aligned one-to-one from the start with all characters of the candidate; timing terms use only adjacent final chars that were consecutive char presses in the record (modifier and navigation presses skipped); two versions, sum and per-term mean of the timing log-likelihood, and A3 on R3-u is their maximum (decision 37); zero timing terms -> timing term 0; a length-only version is reported as secondary; length term = log-likelihood of (replayed char count - candidate char count) under its empirical distribution with additive smoothing, estimated on training logs processed to R3-u and replayed by A1'; the digraph interval table comes from the training logs in R0; the synthetic-log check measures how one replay error degrades the true text's timing term (decision 38)

A4.input: intervals between letter, digit and space presses only
A4.chunk_segments: intervals covering 20 record segments (words) per chunk

attackers.if_A4_reduced: only the A4 rows use the reduced sample; the main table stays at 500 writers

window.defined_on: R0 segments; each form takes the presses inside the window and re-segments
window.A0: window count vs candidate window count
window.A2: also run on R0, R1, R5, R6 in windows
window.A3: on the A2 (A2-b for R3-u) alignment

matching.decoy_pool: all eligible writers of the same prompt except the record's writer (all in the evaluation fold)
matching.negative_control: record swapped with writer B drawn from all writers after exclusion of the same prompt (evaluation fold) (seed use negative_control, one B per record, draw empty); decoys are N - 1 texts drawn with the decoys seed from the pool without B and the record's writer, so there are always N candidates; main forms x strongest attacker x N = 10 and 1000 x full text x 500 writers
matching.window_truth_mismatch: map final-draft words to distributed-text words after whitespace normalisation (word edit-distance alignment); windows whose first word does not map are not used and are counted

columns_added: share of bootstrap resamples per attacker
summary.figure: x = strongest attacker's multiple of 1/N (N = 1000, full text), y = median Spearman with R0 over the fixed set of 10 metrics (see utility.figure_y); describe the Pareto front; no rule recommends a form

utility.baseline: own formulas for R0 and every form (decision 28); Inputlog values only for check 7 (50 writers, Spearman and absolute difference)

formulas.char_count: number of char presses (letter, digit, space, punctuation, enter); R3-u: 'char' presses
formulas.r_burst_mean_len: mean char_count of bursts delineated by an insertion or deletion ([V264] Table 5): a burst ends at a pause > 2000 ms, at a revision or at an insertion away from the leading edge (R0: activity Remove/Cut, Replace, or input with position < current text length; approximations: BackSpace or Delete press, or A1' cursor not at the end)
formulas.within_word_pause_mean: mean pause > 200 ms between two consecutive letter or digit presses
formulas.between_word_pause_mean: mean pause > 200 ms from a word_boundary press to the next letter or digit press (one interval per boundary); intervals from a letter or digit to a separator count in neither
formulas.deletion_mean_len: R0: mean number of characters deleted per deletion run (consecutive Remove/Cut and Replace events summed; [V264] Table 5 'one deletion activity'); approx: run of consecutive BackSpace/Delete presses
formulas.insertion_mean_len: R0: mean run of chars inserted where position < current text length; approx: A1' cursor not at end
formulas.interval_variance_10: standard deviation over the 10 equal time intervals of the active window of (production rate = char presses / interval duration) divided by the task maximum = the maximum interval production rate over all writers after exclusion of the same prompt in R0, the same denominator for every form and sample (decisions 34, 39; [V264] gives no operational definition)

utility.approximations: char count = char presses; deletion = BackSpace and Delete one char each; insertion = char presses when the A1' cursor is not at the end; word boundary = separator presses; R7 counts x 1/(1 - p)

cell_definition.ok: same inputs and formula as R0
cell_definition.approx: computed from other inputs by the approximation rules

utility.random_processing: R5, R6 and R7 random processing once per record, the same processed records as matching
report: median and 10/90 percentiles of ratio to R0
Spearman with human scores, R0 and each form
utility.bootstrap: writer unit, stratified by prompt, 2000 resamples, 95%; same draws as the matching cells of the same sample (500 or all)
utility.sample: summary table and figure: the same 500 writers as the matching main table; all writers after exclusion in the appendix
utility.ratio_zero: writers whose R0 value is 0 or undefined are dropped from that metric's ratio; counts reported per metric and form
utility.figure_y: median Spearman with R0 over the fixed set of 10 metrics; not-computed metrics count as 0; R4 is 0 and annotated

check7.population: writers with Inputlog values in the distribution (all of them if fewer than 50)
check7.revisions: at most one; the revised formula is not re-checked
check7.mismatch: Spearman < 0.9 or median absolute difference > 10% of the R0 median, per metric

exclusion: no Type=IME and no letter Type=insert event
enja15.bootstrap: translator unit, 2000 resamples, 95%; crossed if any translator translated two or more source texts (check 5): resample translators with all their sessions, unstratified, and drop a source text with no record from that resample's mean (count reported); nested if every translator translated one source text: stratify by source text
enja15.question4_wording: 'exceeds' only when the lower bounds of both differences (vs 1/N and vs A0) are above 0 (decision 30)
enja15.question4_form: R3j decides; other forms reported with the same rule; R0j reference only (decision 35)
enja15.question4_level: accuracy, 1/N and A0 accuracy all aggregated the same way (mean over records within each source text, then mean over source texts); differences taken within each bootstrap resample
enja15.A0: record: letter presses among Type=IME or Type=insert events - [Back] presses; text: sum of standard IME keystroke counts of the readings
